fund-manager.label: Fund Manager
fund-manager.role: Managing Partner, Sankofa Capital · Accra & Toronto
fund-manager.quote: “I spent two years trying to get diaspora investors into African deals through traditional SPV structures. The legal fees alone killed most deals before they started. Kori changed everything.”

paragraphs.one: Kofi grew up in Accra, studied finance at the University of Toronto, and spent eight years in Canadian private equity. When he returned to build an Africa-focused investment practice, he hit the wall every diaspora fund manager knows: the infrastructure didn't exist.
paragraphs.two: Wire transfers took 5-7 days and cost 3-4% in fees. Legal structuring for a single SPV ran $15K-$25K. Investor onboarding was manual, fragmented, and slow. He lost three deals in six months because capital couldn't move fast enough.
paragraphs.three: Through Kori, Kofi structured his first SPV in under a week. Smart contracts replaced manual legal coordination. Stablecoin settlement eliminated wire delays. He onboarded 8 investors across 4 countries from a single dashboard — and deployed $480K into SolarGrid Kenya in his first month.
paragraphs.four: Today, Kofi manages 3 active SPVs with $2.4M in AUM across energy, agritech, and edtech. His investors co-invest on identical economic terms, with full on-chain transparency into every milestone and capital release.

angel-investor.label: Angel Investor
angel-investor.quote: “I've wanted to invest in Africa for years. I had the capital, I had the conviction — but I never had a vehicle I could trust. Kori gave me that.”

paragraphs.one: Amara left Ghana at 19 and built a career in Toronto's tech industry. By her mid-thirties she was investing actively in North American startups — and watching African founders solve harder problems with a fraction of the capital.
paragraphs.two: Angel networks in Accra didn't accept diaspora investors. VC funds had $1M minimums. Sending money through informal channels meant zero legal protection and zero visibility into how capital was used.
paragraphs.three: Kori gave Amara a structured, transparent, on-chain vehicle built for diaspora investors. She committed $80K to SolarGrid Kenya through a smart contract that encodes when and how her capital flows.
paragraphs.four: Within three months, she expanded her portfolio to 3 SPVs totaling $185K across energy, edtech, and agritech. She co-invests alongside vetted leads on identical terms.

startup-founder.label: Startup Founder
startup-founder.quote: “Every VC I pitched in San Francisco asked me to ‘explain the Kenya market.’ The diaspora investors on Kori didn't need an explanation — they needed a vehicle. Kori built it.”

paragraphs.one: Wanjiku is a mechanical engineer turned entrepreneur. She spent three years building SolarGrid — a pay-as-you-go solar company deploying off-grid systems across rural Kenya.
paragraphs.two: Western VCs didn't understand the market. Local bank lending rates sat at 30-50%. She applied to six accelerators, got into two, and raised nothing.
paragraphs.three: Through Kori, Wanjiku connected with a lead investor who understood off-grid energy from the inside. Within weeks, 8 diaspora co-investors committed $480K through a SAFE, settled in stablecoins.
paragraphs.four: Smart contracts encoded 4 milestones, each releasing a tranche upon validator confirmation. She hit her first two milestones early, deploying 50 solar units and receiving $280K directly to her wallet.
paragraphs.five: Today, SolarGrid is preparing to scale to 200 installations across 3 counties. Her third milestone — revenue validation — is under review. She's building with clarity, not chaos.
